brief.headline: We're 1.36% of their sales (₹15.03 Cr of ₹1102.11 Cr) — use that weight to secure faster payment in exchange for a modest price cut

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 3–5% price cut to bring us closer to the India export unit value benchmark
priceAsk.target: Move from ₹66.48/KG toward the ₹42.95/kg export benchmark — a target of ₹63–64/KG would save us roughly ₹35–52 L per year
priceAsk.basis: Our price sits in the ₹66–73/kg typical band (market-fair), but the India export unit value is ₹42.95/kg. Even a modest move toward that line is defensible, and we have three credible backup makers to leverage

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (move from 30 days to 15 days after receipt) in exchange for part of the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster costs us ₹61.76 L in cash — use that as a trade for a price concession worth the same or more

brief.financialLeverage: They keep only ₹2.30 of every ₹100 they sell (2.3% profit), so they have very little room to absorb a deep price cut. But they owe ₹238.85 Cr at 2.25 times their own cash — debt is heavy, so getting paid faster is valuable to them. We're a big customer at 1.36% of their ₹1102.11 Cr revenue (₹15.03 Cr spend), so we have real weight. Push confidently on payment speed for a price trade, but don't squeeze so hard on price alone that we risk their ability to deliver steady supply — their health score is D (21/100), signalling some fragility.

evidence.point: We are a significant customer to them
evidence.figure: Our ₹15.03 Cr is 1.36% of their ₹1102.11 Cr revenue

evidence.point: Their profit margin is very tight

evidence.figure: Debt is 2.25x their own cash, totalling ₹238.85 Cr

evidence.point: Our price is above the India export reference
evidence.figure: We pay ₹66.48/KG; India export unit value is ₹42.95/kg

evidence.point: Market pricing shows room to negotiate
evidence.figure: Anhydrous Dextrose IP asking band is ₹60–81/kg, typical ₹66–73/kg — verdict: MARKET-FAIR (slightly favourable)

evidence.point: Faster payment has real value to us as a trade chip
evidence.figure: Paying 15 days faster frees ₹61.76 L of our cash — use it to negotiate a matching or larger price cut

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker with ₹2359.06 Cr revenue and a B (62/100) health score — an established dextrose supplier and a strong drop-in alternate

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore maize wet-miller producing Dextrose ANHYDROUS (IV-fluid grade) — exact form match; ₹365.39 Cr revenue, confirm IP monograph CoA before switching

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (starch, dextrose) with ₹821.13 Cr revenue and C (53/100) health — growing capacity, a credible second source

risks: Their health score is D (21/100) and they owe 2.25 times their own cash — push too hard on price and we may destabilise a supplier already under strain
Profit margin is only 2.3%, so a big price cut eats into what little cushion they have — focus the ask on payment speed (which costs them less) rather than price alone
We currently pay ₹66.48/KG, already at the best price we have across vendors — any cut needs a clear trade (faster payment) and a credible alternate lined up to make it stick
Three strong alternates exist (Gulshan, Tirupati, Sanstar), but each needs qualification and CoA review before we can switch — start that process now so the backup is real, not just a threat
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership — you're our sole Dextrose supplier at ₹15.03 Cr a year — and we'd like to find a way to pay you faster in exchange for moving our price a bit closer to the ₹42.95/kg export benchmark.
